name: Hotel Principe di Savoia Milano
positioning: Hotel Principe di Savoia, a Dorchester Collection hotel on Milan's Piazza della Repubblica that first opened in 1927
best_for: Travelers who want a central Milan base near the Repubblica metro and Stazione Centrale
Guests who want a hotel spa with an indoor pool, sauna and an outdoor terrace

facts.text: The hotel originally opened in 1927 as Principe e Savoia.
The hotel is at Piazza della Repubblica 17 in Milan, in the centre of Porta Nuova.
The hotel is a 2-minute walk from the Repubblica metro station.
The hotel is 10 minutes from Milan's main train station, Stazione Centrale.
The Club 10 Fitness & Beauty Center has an indoor pool, hydro massage room, steam room, sauna, outdoor terrace, gym and spa.
The Technogym gym looks out over the city skyline.
The Deluxe Room has high ceilings and hand-painted frescoes.
The Imperial Suites were designed by architect Celeste Dell'Anna and feature Art Deco accents.
Acanto Restaurant's chef Matteo Gabrielli comes from Varese, and his cooking is rooted in Lombard traditions.
Acanto Restaurant's large windows look onto an Italian garden with a fountain.
Il Salotto serves an afternoon tea with a Milanese twist built around local delicacies.
Guests get a complimentary shuttle to the city centre in a Mercedes-Benz Viano.

highlights.text: The Presidential Suite has its own Pompeian-style private swimming pool and spa.
Tavolo Cristallo is a private table surrounded by a veil of Swarovski crystals.
Club 10 has a terrace where guests can watch the sunset over Milan after a spa ritual.
Principe Bar hosts board game nights every Monday and Tuesday.
Principe Bar has its own gin, made by Cillario & Marazzi Spirits Co.

considerations.text: Conde Nast Traveler reports the hotel will close on January 1, 2027, for an extensive restoration and is expected to reopen in 2029.
Children under 16 must be accompanied by an adult to use the pool.
WhataHotel notes premium luxury pricing reflects the high-end positioning.
